title: First night at Lincoln: Bud Rankin offers a $10 gig
summary: On his first Sunday, Bud Rankin, an older student, offered Thomas a $10 gig at Moreau. Thomas turned it down for fear of being sent home.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

was going on, it's a pretty rugged deal and the family needed some help.
Well, when you get there, Joe, how long were you going to be there, how many years?
Well, you know, high schook, four years. I hope to make it through the four years, you know.
Now you get any musical tuition there?
None.
Did they have a band there?
May I give you my introduction to Lincoln?
Yeah.

The first night there, it was on a Sunday and I must have gotten there around 5 or 6 o'clock ... I met a tremendous fellow who am there whom I, I'm the kid in short pants. But, he had a gig at a place called Moreau. I don't know why I'll never forget it. His name was Bud Rankin.
What was the name of the place?
Moreau - M-o-r-e-a-u.
Oh, yes, a French name.

Yeah, it was out on the highway right past Cottage Farm, I mean they're from Cottage Farm because I was in high school. And, this idea being in my mind so much about, see things were very strict in those days. Where I was raised of strict up to a point, I was always allowed a certain amount of leeway. After they found out what they were whipping into me, they stuck with me and there could be any little violation and
JTHOMAS (1)
that night I was offered a gig.
The first day you were there?

My first day, my very first day I was there. And, what happened was they had this one dormitory was being built so we all stayed in the study hall. So this guy comes in. He says, "I heard there's a cornet player in the house." So I -how's he going to have heard of me?- waited ... so he kept on talking so I said, "I'm Joe Thomas. maybe I play cornet." He said, "Yeah, maybe you're the guy I'm looking for." So I said, "What's your name." He said, "Well, I'm Bud Rankin." I said, "Hi, Mr. Rankin."
He was older than you?

Oh, yeah. Bud was a tremendous athlete. He was in college. So he said, I've got a little gig and if you can get out tonight, I mean, there'll be no trouble for you. So I said, "No, Mr. Rankin, I can't make it." "Ten dollars." So he said, "Why can't you make it?" I said, "Well, I just left home and now if I get sent back home Before." And he said, "Well, you haven't even registered. Who knows you're here?" And I said, "Well, you did." He said xthere would be no problem at all. We'd go out and work a couple of hours and come home. "I'll bring you back." So I didn't make it.
Oh, you didn't?
No, man. Send me back home, hadn't even opened. Closed before I opened, never happen. And, that was my first tempting. You kidding, 10 dollars. It was very tempting.
